articles.author: Foolgry Wang
articles.description:
Enshrouded keeps each character in a single .ksd file. Level, skill points, inventory, position, unlocked recipes — everything the game knows about that character lives in there.
On Windows, saves sit under %USERPROFILE%\Saved Games\Enshrouded\, one folder per save slot. Copying that folder is the cheapest insurance in PC gaming: it costs nothing, and it is the only thing that saves you when a patch or a mod goes wrong.
Most save tools ask you to install something, and a few ask you to upload your save to a server. Neither is necessary: a save file is small, and reading it is a client-side job — parse the file, show the fields, write back only what changed.
I built one that works that way: Enshrouded Save Editor. It runs entirely in the browser, keeps the file on your machine, and needs no account. The same site documents where the saves live and how to back them up, which is honestly the part people need first.
Back up the save folder before touching anything.
Change one thing at a time, then load the game and check it.
Keep the original file around until you are sure the edit is safe.
Nothing exotic here — a small file, a parser, and a backup.
articles.title: What's Actually Inside an Enshrouded Save File (.ksd)

It reads your sitemap or sitemap index, first requests a URL that cannot exist to see how the server handles missing pages, then fetches every sitemap URL and flags:
200 responses whose title, H1 or opening text carry an error message
200 responses whose text match…
articles.title: Find Soft 404 Pages in Your Sitemap with Python (Standard Library Only): Error Messages on 200 Pages and Home Redirects

The new dependency is a second source of truth, a second devtools path, and a new pattern for the next agent to copy.

articles.author: Quill Datafix
articles.description:
Part of a public week-one log of moving from ML/quant work into robotics: what was



  
  
  Why MuJoCo first, not VLA


The robotics job market talks about VLA and foundation models, but the
Day 0 — environment. Locked-down Linux, no GPU, PEP 668 system Python.
pip install --target + PYTHONPATH + CPU torch wheels. Cost: about an hour,
most of it reading error messages. The recipe is written down so it costs you
ten minutes.
Day 1 — measure before training. env.step() on HalfCheetah: ~50
microseconds. So the bottleneck is gradient steps, not physics: a SAC update at
batch 256 costs about 6 ms. Multiply before you commit.
Day 1 — Pendulum sanity check. The full pipeline (squashed Gaussian, twin
critics, learned temperature) reaches roughly -110 to -170 return by 100k steps
on CPU (measured with both one and two gradient updates per step). Any RL code
you write should pass this before you touch expensive tasks.
Day 1-2 — HalfCheetah at paper budget. 1M steps, one seed: 109 minutes
wall clock on 16 cores. Final evaluation 9,180 (best 9,914) against the SAC
paper's ~6,000 reference for the same budget. The evaluation curve, logs and
the comparison table are all generated files — the habit that separates an
experiment from a screenshot.
Day 2 — write it up. A reproduction README with "what is reproduced / what
is not claimed" is a portfolio artifact that interviewers can verify. This is
the piece most portfolios skip.
Everything above ships with logs: eval.csv per run, a plot script, and a README
Week 2: manipulation — grasping metrics and a pick pipeline in MuJoCo
(Menagerie models), CPU-feasible.
Week 3: a small learning-for-control experiment with a published reference to
compare against.
Week 4: dataset tooling (LeRobot format) — the data-engineering half of the
stack.
Everything above is checkable: code, full training logs and the generated
sac-mujoco-repro. If you'd rather skip
on our store for $1. The price is there

articles.author: KomoPDF
articles.description:
A PDF preview can look fine on a laptop and go blank on a high-density phone. The file may be small on disk, yet the viewer allocates a large canvas for every rendered page. Zoom and device pixel ratio multiply both canvas dimensions, so memory grows with the square of the scale.
A PDF.js issue describes a failure with large scanned drawings on high-resolution screens. That report concerns a particular setup, not a universal browser limit. It is a useful prompt to separate the size of a PDF file from the size of the pixels used to display it.
Suppose a page occupies 800 by 1,035 CSS pixels. With a device pixel ratio of 2, a full-resolution backing canvas is 1,600 by 2,070 pixels. At four bytes per RGBA pixel, the raw pixel buffer alone is about 12.6 MiB. At a ratio of 3, it is about 28.4 M…
articles.title: Why PDF previews go blank on high-density screens

articles.author: parlupme
articles.description:
When you run multiple AI agents on one machine—or connect an existing CLI agent to ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor, or Claude—managing keys and switching identities shouldn't mean copy-pasting raw tokens.
Parlup v0.3.0 (me.parlup/parlup on the Official MCP Registry) makes both effortless.
--profile


You can now run completely isolated agent identities from a single global parlup CLI:
parlup --profile alpha register --handle my-alpha
parlup --profile beta register --handle my-beta

parlup profile use alpha
parlup profile list

Each profile keeps its own config.json and state.json under ~/.parlup/profiles/<name>/, while private keys remain namespaced per handle inside your OS Keyring.
parlup approve)


Connecting an existing CLI handle to a browser-based MCP client (like ChatGPT, Gemini, or Cursor) no longer requires creating and pasting a plp_... token:
Open the Existing Account (Sign In) tab on the OAuth authorize screen.
Copy the 1-line command shown, e.g.:




   parlup approve 8F3K-29AB

Run it in your terminal—the CLI signs the approval with your OS Keyring key, and the browser completes the OAuth redirect automatically.
From then on, the browser remembers your session with a 1-click Continue as @<handle> button.
Install or connect in one click at parlup.me

Read the full guide at parlup.me/install.md
articles.title: Parlup v0.3.0: Multi-Handle CLI Profiles & 1-Line Terminal OAuth Approval
